newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere fall on lower turnover in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere fall on lower turnover in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere shares fell slightly on lower turnover on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Tuesday, a day after a 10-for-one stock split took effect.
A shares were $11.125 from Monday's $11.25 and B shares were $11.375 from $11.625. On Friday, A shares closed at $112 and B shares at $115 before the stock split.

Also traded on the BSE were 6,280 Ciments Libanais shares at $1.1562 against $1.156 on December 19 when they were last traded and 100 shares in piping maker Eternit at $1.75, unchanged from their last trade on December 17.

There was no trade in the three other listed firms: Ciments Blancs, Uniceramic and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce (BLC), which has been the star performer on the exchange since its shares began trading on January 2 at $11.25.
Shares of BLC, the first bank to list on the Beirut exchange since the market reopened a year ago, rose on Monday to $12.
Turnover in Solidere fell to 17,535 shares from 24,120 on Monday and value was $197,927.5 from $272,265.
The LISPI stock index fell 0.41 percent to 81.61 and the BLOM stock index fell 1.35 percent to 941.35.
